name: jungle_depths_mapstyle_c
prompt:
16-bit pixel art style-tuning sheet for a top-down bomberman-style DEEP JUNGLE stage. Exactly 4 separate mini-map panels in a neat 2x2 grid on one flat plain cream background (#F7F1E3). Each panel is ONE complete 10x10 tile map seen from directly above like a board-game board, same scale and camera, equal quarter, generous margin, nothing crossing between panels. No labels, no text, no numbers, no watermark, no UI, no characters. Every map is a dense ancient-tree courtyard: pale jade-green stone pavers overgrown with light grass and roots, giant ancient tree trunks and massive roots along all four edges, many young trees and bushes, 7-11 destructible tree-type blocks (cut logs, leafy sapling blocks, bush blocks), and exactly one 3x2 hollow ancient tree-trunk gate. Tiny snake carving on one block only. Crisp hand-placed pixels, 1px selective dark-green outline, flat cel shading 2-3 tones, top-left light, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no drop shadows.

REFERENCE USE: the LEFT half of the reference image shows the STRUCTURE and STYLE to follow (ancient tree courtyard, pale stone pavers, giant roots, hollow trunk gate). The RIGHT half shows a brighter sunlit look; use its brightness as the upper limit but tone it down slightly. Do NOT copy its meadow floor; keep the ancient-tree courtyard structure.

PALETTE: fresh light green daylight. Pale mint green, soft sage, young leaf green, cream-white highlights, mid-green accents, warm brown bark, thin dark green outline. Never dark teal, never muddy brown, never heavy black shadows, never washed-out white.

EXPOSURE LADDER - the four panels show the SAME style with only brightness and contrast changed, increasing left-to-right, top-to-bottom:
TOP-LEFT panel = level 1: the closest to the darker left reference, but with shadows gently lifted; soft dim daylight, still a little subdued.
TOP-RIGHT panel = level 2: medium-soft daylight, clearly brighter than level 1, low contrast, comfortable.
BOTTOM-LEFT panel = level 3: the RECOMMENDED balanced look; fresh pale-green late-morning light, bright but soft, shadows only 1-2 tones darker than the lit stone, nothing overexposed.
BOTTOM-RIGHT panel = level 4: the brightest, close to the right reference, but highlights toned down so no area turns pure white and no detail is lost.

RULES: identical tile scale, outline weight, detail level and palette family across all four panels; only exposure and contrast differ. Keep the overall tone light green and airy. Every walkable cell must read clearly differently from every blocking cell.
